events.continuity_hook: Final pre-trip check for the Philadelphia client kickoff after the closer hotel and Thursday return were approved.
events.interaction_goal: Create a concise Philadelphia travel checklist and identify the last items Maya should verify before leaving for the airport.
events.scenario_brief: A few days before the Philadelphia kickoff, Maya has the Monday afternoon ATL-to-PHL nonstop, Thursday afternoon return, and campus-adjacent refundable hotel booked. The client sends visitor instructions showing badge pickup at 8:00 a.m., construction around one campus entrance, and luggage storage available on Thursday. The hotel breakfast will be paid separately, but there are nearby quick options and an on-site restaurant for the arrival night. She wants a final rundown for Atlanta airport timing, PHL-to-hotel transfer choices, quiet-room and luggage-hold requests, breakfast timing before the first client session, receipt handling, and whether any better window seat has opened. The only unresolved items are whether to use rideshare or rail from the airport and whether winter weather should add extra buffer.

events.continuity_hook: Starts a new training-travel episode after the Philadelphia client trip wraps up.
events.interaction_goal: Frame the Minneapolis trip, identify workable flight windows and hotel areas, and list the details Maya needs before sending a plan for approval.
events.scenario_brief: After returning from Philadelphia, Maya is asked to attend a regional reporting-and-configuration training in Minneapolis from Monday, March 23 through Thursday, March 26. The training will be downtown, with required sessions Tuesday and Wednesday, a likely Thursday half-day, and an optional Monday evening welcome dinner that is not yet confirmed. She wants Atlanta flights with straightforward routing, a hotel that keeps cold-weather morning logistics simple, and enough dining access that she is not stuck searching after a late workday. The unresolved pieces are whether she needs to arrive in time for the Monday dinner, whether the company has a rate at the attached downtown hotel, and whether Thursday ends early enough for an afternoon return.

events.continuity_hook: Continues the Minneapolis planning after the schedule becomes firmer and Monday no longer requires a Sunday arrival.
events.interaction_goal: Compare the main flight-and-hotel combinations, weigh the attached hotel against the breakfast-included alternative, and choose the package to route for approval.
events.scenario_brief: The training organizer confirms an 8:30 a.m. Tuesday start, required sessions through Wednesday afternoon, and a Thursday noon wrap-up. The Monday welcome dinner is optional but useful for meeting the trainers. Maya is comparing a Monday morning Delta nonstop that arrives around midday with a cheaper one-stop itinerary that lands close to dinner, while a Sunday evening arrival would add another hotel night. Hotel choices include the attached downtown conference hotel with strong ratings and on-site dining but paid breakfast, an extended-stay hotel with included breakfast a longer walk away, and a slightly cheaper property near restaurants but outside the easiest skyway route. Thursday has both an afternoon nonstop and an early evening nonstop. She is deciding whether convenience near the training site is worth the higher hotel rate.

events.continuity_hook: Keeps the Minneapolis episode moving after the flight and hotel plan is approved but the Thursday afternoon schedule becomes less settled.
events.interaction_goal: Decide whether to move the return to the early evening nonstop and prepare a brief rationale for the schedule cushion before fares change.
events.scenario_brief: Maya's manager approves the Monday morning nonstop and the attached downtown hotel for the Minneapolis training. A new note from the training team adds an optional Thursday lab from 1:00 to 3:30 p.m. that may be useful if the new reporting module is covered. Her current draft return is an afternoon nonstop that would require leaving soon after the formal wrap-up, while an early evening nonstop gives enough cushion for the lab but gets her home later. One-stop returns are available but do not save enough to justify the added moving parts. Seat selection is also getting tighter, with only a few window seats left toward the back of the plane.

events.continuity_hook: Final pre-trip check for the Minneapolis training after the return was moved later to protect the Thursday schedule.
events.interaction_goal: Build a compact Minneapolis travel checklist and flag the few items Maya should recheck the day before travel.
events.scenario_brief: A few days before departure, Maya has the Monday morning nonstop, the attached downtown hotel, and the early evening Thursday return booked. The training agenda is final, with the Thursday lab still optional but now likely worth attending. A late-season snow shower is possible on arrival day, and the hotel confirms dining on-site but no included breakfast. She wants a final logistics pass covering Atlanta airport timing, MSP-to-downtown transportation, hotel check-in, indoor walking routes to the training rooms, breakfast workarounds, dinner options for the first night, receipts for ground transport, and whether the booked seats are still the best available.

events.continuity_hook: Starts a new family leisure episode after the March work-travel block.
events.interaction_goal: Frame the San Antonio family trip, compare the first airport and hotel-area choices, and identify what Maya needs to confirm with her spouse before narrowing options.
events.scenario_brief: After the Minneapolis training, Maya starts planning a short family spring-break trip to San Antonio with her spouse and child. They are looking at Wednesday, April 8 through Sunday, April 12, but her spouse may only be able to take Thursday and Friday off. She wants simple Atlanta-to-San Antonio flights, a return that does not burn the whole Sunday, and a well-rated hotel that keeps sightseeing, dinner, and mornings easy. The main hotel question is whether to pay more for a River Walk location with paid breakfast or choose a roomier breakfast-included hotel a bit farther out. The unresolved pieces are the exact departure day, whether a pool matters enough for the child, and whether the nonstop fares stay reasonable for three travelers.
